title: Motor Transport Operations Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
10.     MOS 3537, Motor Transport Operations Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. A Motor Transport Operations Chief is responsible to the
commander and assists in the planning, training, licensing, deployment and
employment of all operator/crew level maintenance. Also responsible for the
planning and execution of motor transport operations, directs the activities
of all 353X enlisted personnel in a motor pool, conducts motor vehicles
accident/mishap investigations and prepares accident/mishap reports. The
Motor Transport Operations Chief coordinates the preparation and assignment
of motor transport personnel/equipment in accordance with the table of
organization/table of equipment of their unit. The Motor Transport Operation



                                         3-288                         Enclosure (1)
 3129                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



Chief acts as the fleet manager, truck transportation coordinator, and
assists with all duties and responsibilities under the cognizance of the
Motor Transport Officer.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must hold MOS 3531 as a primary MOS.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Motor Transport Staff Noncommissioned Officer
Operations Course (MTSNCOOC) (M03CDL7) conducted at Marine Corps Combat
Service Support School, Camp Lejeune, NC, which is required within one year
of promotion to the rank of Staff Sergeant unless assigned outside the MOS in
a supporting establishment command such as recruiting/drill instructor/MSG
duty/Combat instructor. In these cases, upon reassignment to a billet
requiring MOS 3537, the Marines will be required to attend the MTSNCOOC
within one year. Failure to complete this course, within the designated time
frame may result in being considered less than fully qualified to the rank of
gunnery sergeant.

        (2) Must maintain a valid U.S. Government Vehicle Operator's
Identification Card (OF-346) qualified to operate MTVR 7 ton and LVSR (GySgt
to SSgt).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Transportation and Material-Moving Machine
and Vehicle Op 53-1031.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Semitrailer Refueler Operator, 3534.

            (2) Vehicle Recovery Operator, 3536.




                                         3-289                       Enclosure (1)
 3130                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
